description: An envelope that rises to one level, holds there, then falls to another, in 4HP, with the time and the curve of each ramp set separately

params.text: Chooses how the Phase input is read: as a gate whose rising edge attacks and whose falling edge releases, or as a trigger where they alternate
Starts the delay and release by hand
Makes each attack trigger start a fresh attack from the release level, instead of carrying on from wherever the envelope is
Makes each release trigger restart the delay, instead of being ignored while the delay or release is already running
Sets how long the envelope holds its level between the attack and the release, 0 to 10 seconds
Sets how quickly the envelope covers the whole distance between the two levels on the way up, 0 to 10 seconds
Sets how quickly the envelope covers the whole distance between the two levels on the way down, 0 to 10 seconds
Bends the rise, concave one way and convex the other, with a straight line in the centre
Bends the fall, concave one way and convex the other, with a straight line in the centre
Sets the voltage the attack climbs to and holds at, -10V to +10V, and 10V unless you move it
Sets the voltage the release falls to and holds at, -10V to +10V, and 0V unless you move it
Links the release time knob to the attack time knob, so the release knob greys out and follows it
Links the release shape knob to the attack shape knob, green for the same value and red for the mirror image of it

inputs.text: Drives both stages from one signal: in gate mode the rising edge attacks and the falling edge releases, in trigger mode they take turns
A rising edge starts an attack; a light beside it is green while the rise runs and red while the envelope is held at the attack level
A rising edge starts the delay and then the release; a light beside it is yellow during the delay, green during the fall and red once the release level is reached

outputs.text: Fires a 2ms pulse as an attack starts, at the gate-high level from the menu rather than the trigger-high level
Fires a 2ms pulse when the rise reaches the attack level, and not if the attack is cut short
Fires a 2ms pulse as the release starts, which is after the delay has run
Fires a 2ms pulse when the fall reaches the release level, and not if the release is cut short
Carries the envelope itself, between the two level knobs

notes: the time knobs set a rate, not a duration: they say how long the full distance between the two levels takes, so a ramp starting part way there finishes sooner
an interrupted stage starts the next one from wherever the envelope is, unless the matching retrigger setting is on
patching the end-of-attack output back into the release trigger makes one attack trigger run a whole cycle, and adding end-of-release back into the attack trigger makes it run on by itself
this module is monophonic, and comes up sitting at the release level waiting for an attack
menu: Attack rate chaos, Delay rate chaos, Release rate chaos — picks a new random length for that stage each time it begins, up to a tenth or ten times the dialled time at 100%
Process quality: Audio, High, Balanced, Low, Very low — sets how often the module runs its algorithm, from every cycle down to every 256th; below Balanced a 1ms trigger can be missed
Gate-high detect-level — sets the voltage at which an incoming gate counts as high, 1V or more unless you change it
Gate-high output-level — sets the voltage a gate output carries while high, 10V unless you change it
Gate-low output-level — sets the voltage a gate output carries while low, 0V unless you change it
Trigger-high detect-level — sets the voltage at which an incoming trigger counts as high, 1V or more unless you change it
Trigger-low detect-level — sets the voltage an incoming trigger must fall back below before the next one is counted, under 0.1V unless you change it
Trigger-high output-level — sets the voltage a trigger pulse carries during its 1ms high phase, 10V unless you change it
Trigger-low output-level — sets the voltage a trigger output carries between pulses, 0V unless you change it

inputs.0:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads the rising edge of the Phase input; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.2:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads the falling edge of the Phase input; a negative voltage does nothing here.
